# Exact projective identities for median transport

Write `n=1`, fix an integer `z0`, and choose `y=(z0,x0)∈C`. Let `K_z` denote the continuous fiber. For integers `k≥1`, define

`N_k^±=(K_(z0±k)−x0)/k`.

## Nested sets and convex gauges

For `ℓ≥k`, convexity and the segment from `y` to a point in the `ℓ`th fiber give `N_ℓ^±⊂N_k^±`.

Let `D=C−y` and let `p_D(v)=inf{λ>0:v∈λD}` be its extended-valued gauge. Because `D` is compact, convex, and contains zero, its gauge is convex and is positive on nonzero vectors wherever finite. Put

`h_±(a)=p_D(±1,a)`.

These functions are extended convex functions, and

`N_k^±={a:h_±(a)≤1/k}`.

The equality follows directly from homogeneity of the gauge and the fact that `D` is closed and stable under contractions toward zero. It does not require `y` to be an interior point of `C`.

## Directional pushforward density

Project a source point `(z0±k,x)` to `a=(x−x0)/k`. The pushforward of unnormalized mixed-integer volume on the strict side has Lebesgue density

`f_±(a)=Σ_(k≥1) k^d 1_(N_k^±)(a)`.

Only finitely many terms occur, because `C` is bounded. Consequently

`∫ f_± = Σ_(k≥1) vol_d(K_(z0±k))`,

and

`∫ a f_±(a) da = Σ_(k≥1) (1/k) ∫_(K_(z0±k)) (x−x0) dx`.

The factors are exactly the Jacobian `dx=k^d da` and the additional factor `1/k` for the first moment.

If `F_d(m)=Σ_(k=1)^m k^d`, then nesting gives

`f_±(a)=F_d(floor(1/h_±(a)))`,

with value zero when no positive integer is admissible. Hence every superlevel set of `f_±` is convex.

## The halfspace sign loses its radial coefficients

Suppose a left source point has `x−x0=k a` and a right source point has `x'−x0=ℓ b`. Their segment intersects the selected fiber at

`T−x0 = [kℓ/(k+ℓ)](a+b)`.

The coefficient is strictly positive. Thus, for a halfspace whose boundary passes through `y`, target membership depends only on the sign of the corresponding linear functional of `a+b`, independent of `k,ℓ`.

Every coupling of the directional measures can be lifted to the original source measures: conditional on a direction `a`, use index `k` with weight proportional to `k^d1_(N_k)(a)`. This yields the prescribed source marginals and the displayed sign identity.

## Opposite-direction matching equals the usual symmetric overlap

The greatest mass that can be coupled with `a+b=0` is

`I=∫ min(f_−(a),f_+(−a)) da`.

The pointwise minimum is both necessary, by marginal domination, and sufficient, by coupling that density at `(a,−a)`. Nestedness and the common cumulative weights imply

`min(f_−(a),f_+(−a)) = Σ_(k≥1) k^d 1_(N_k^−∩(−N_k^+))(a)`.

Therefore

`I=Σ_(k≥1) vol_d(K_(z0−k)∩(2x0−K_(z0+k)))`.

Allowing different source distances in the directional matching does not improve this total over ordinary centrally reflected mixed-fiber overlap. A stronger route must use the unmatched directional geometry, not just this diagonal matching mass.

## The densities are not power-concave

For `C=[−2,2]×[−1,1]^d` and `y=0`, let `K=[−1,1]^d`. On either strict side,

`f=1_K+2^d1_(K/2)`.

This has an interior downward jump. At the points with first coordinates `.49` and `.53` and other coordinates zero, the values are `1+2^d` and `1`, whereas their midpoint has value `1`. Every finite power mean of those two positive endpoint values is strictly greater than one. Thus no finite power-concavity, including log-concavity, follows from the projective nesting. Quasiconcavity is the precise property established here.

## A legitimate harmonic-weighted candidate in the balanced case

Suppose the strict-left and strict-right masses are equal and positive. Write their fiber volumes as `w_(±k)` and centroids as `c_(±k)`. The choice

`x0 = [Σ_(±,k) (w_(±k)/k)c_(±k)]/[Σ_(±,k) w_(±k)/k]`

makes the combined directional first moment zero. It also gives a valid point of the selected fiber: the same convex combination of the source centroids has integer coordinate

`z0 + [Σ_right w − Σ_left w]/[Σ_(±,k) w/k] = z0`.

Convexity places that barycenter in `C`. This establishes membership, not a halfspace-depth guarantee. The case of unequal strict-side masses and central-fiber allocation is not settled by this formula.
